title: "What assumptions have we made so far, can you rank them by severity?"
---


Each assumption is swapped for the other readings the plan allows, one at a
time with everything else held fixed at 6 m/s, and severity is read as the
spread it opens in the nose ballast needed for 10% MAC — the conclusion this
chapter has actually drawn. Two assumptions cannot be tested this way and are
named in the answer instead.

::: {#9baed1b9 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
ALPHA = np.linspace(-15, 15, 121)


def assess(airplane, x_ref, mp, band=(0, 8), V=6.0):
    """Neutral point, best L/D, and the nose ballast for 10% MAC."""
    p = polars(ALPHA, V=V, airplane=airplane)
    CL, CD, Cm = np.array(p["CL"]), np.array(p["CD"]), np.array(p["Cm"])
    k = (ALPHA >= band[0]) & (ALPHA <= band[1])
    x_np = x_ref - np.polyfit(CL[k], Cm[k], 1)[0] * c_w
    x_cg = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
    return x_np, (CL / CD).max(), mp.mass * (mp.x_cg - x_cg) / x_cg


def wing_at(x_le, curved_is_le=False, tip_rise=None):
    """The wing rebuilt at a chosen root LE station, optionally flipped."""
    rise = z_tip if tip_rise is None else tip_rise
    return asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
        asb.WingXSec(
            xyz_le=[x_le + ((wing_c[0] - c) if curved_is_le else 0),
                    eta * b_w / 2, eta * rise],
            chord=c, airfoil=airfoil,
        )
        for eta, c in zip(wing_eta, wing_c)
    ])


def with_wing(wing, x_ref):
    base = build_airplane()
    return asb.Airplane(
        name="variant", wings=[wing] + list(base.wings[1:]),
        fuselages=base.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w,
        xyz_ref=[x_ref, 0, 0],
    )


def mass_with_wing_at(x_le):
    """The wing carries mass as well as lift, so moving it moves the CG."""
    global x_le_w
    saved, x_le_w = x_le_w, x_le
    try:
        return mass_properties()
    finally:
        x_le_w = saved
```

``` {.python .cell-code}
mp0 = mass_properties()
base = assess(mceagle, x_qc_w, mp0)

cases = {}

# The "Mount wings here" bracket runs 119.2 to 166.4 mm aft of the nose -- 47 mm
# against a 99 mm root chord, so it cannot be marking the chord. The model
# centres the chord on it; the alternatives pin one end of the chord instead.
cases["wing station on its mount bracket"] = [
    assess(with_wing(wing_at(xl), xl + 0.25 * wing_c[0]),
           xl + 0.25 * wing_c[0], mass_with_wing_at(xl))
    for xl in [0.1664 - wing_c[0], 0.1192]
]

# "A slight negative angle to the plane of the wings", with no number given.
cases["stabilizer incidence, 0 to -4 deg"] = [
    assess(build_airplane(stab_incidence=inc), x_qc_w, mp0)
    for inc in [0.0, -4.0]
]

# 5 mm foam on the mean chord is 5.7% thick; the section stands in for a flat
# plate, and the sheet thickness that picks it is itself assumed.
_af = airfoil
cases["section standing in for flat foam"] = []
for _name in ["naca0004", "naca0008"]:
    airfoil = asb.Airfoil(_name)
    cases["section standing in for flat foam"].append(
        assess(build_airplane(), x_qc_w, mp0))
airfoil = _af

# The wing is traced with one straight edge and one curved; which is the
# leading edge is a reading of the plan, not a measurement. Flipping it also
# moves the wing's own centroid, hence the mass offset.
cases["which wing edge is the leading edge"] = [
    base,
    assess(with_wing(wing_at(x_le_w, curved_is_le=True), x_qc_w), x_qc_w,
           mass_with_wing_at(x_le_w + wing_c[0] - 2 * 0.0450)),
]

# The neutral point comes from a straight-line fit whose band is a choice.
cases["neutral-point fit band"] = [
    assess(mceagle, x_qc_w, mp0, band=b) for b in [(0, 6), (2, 10)]
]

# Glue is not in the mass build-up at all. It lies where the fuselage lies.
cases["glue, currently not modelled"] = [
    (base[0], base[1],
     (mp0.mass + m) * ((mp0 + asb.MassProperties(mass=m, x_cg=0.1163)).x_cg
                       - (base[0] - 0.10 * c_w)) / (base[0] - 0.10 * c_w))
    for m in [0.0, 3.0e-3]
]

cases["operating speed, 4 to 8 m/s"] = [
    assess(mceagle, x_qc_w, mp0, V=V) for V in [4.0, 8.0]
]

# The plan's 2.5 cm tip rise, scaled as an angle or kept as a length.
cases["dihedral, 9.6 or 13.3 deg"] = [
    base, assess(with_wing(wing_at(x_le_w, tip_rise=0.025), x_qc_w), x_qc_w, mp0)
]

_shape = fus_shape
cases["fuselage cross-section exponent"] = []
for fus_shape in [2.0, 10.0]:
    cases["fuselage cross-section exponent"].append(
        assess(build_airplane(), x_qc_w, mp0))
fus_shape = _shape

print(f"baseline: x_np {base[0]*1e3:.1f} mm, best L/D {base[1]:.2f}, "
      f"ballast {base[2]*1e3:.2f} g\n")
print(f"{'assumption':38s} {'x_np [mm]':>16s} {'L/D':>13s} {'ballast [g]':>14s}")
order = sorted(cases, key=lambda k: -abs(cases[k][1][2] - cases[k][0][2]))
for k in order:
    (n0, l0, b0), (n1, l1, b1) = cases[k]
    print(f"{k:38s} {n0*1e3:7.1f}{n1*1e3:8.1f} {l0:6.2f}{l1:7.2f}"
          f" {b0*1e3:6.2f}{b1*1e3:7.2f}")
```

**Answer.** No single assumption dominates. Five sit within a factor of about
2.5 of one another and together set the answer; below them the rest are noise.

Largest is where the wing sits along the fuselage: the plan's mount bracket is
47 mm long against a 99 mm root chord, so it cannot be marking the chord, and
the readings it permits move the neutral point between 135.2 and 178.0 mm — the
neutral point tracks the wing at about 0.83 mm per mm — and the ballast between
4.59 and 1.99 g. Then, in order: the stabilizer incidence, which the plan
describes only as "a slight negative angle" (1.80–3.71 g); the fit band chosen
for the neutral point (1.92–3.55 g); the section standing in for flat foam,
together with the 5 mm thickness that picks it (2.44–3.70 g); and which of the
wing's two edges is the leading one (2.10–3.10 g). That the fit band — a
choice made in the analysis, not in the aircraft — ranks third is worth noting.
Glue, absent from the mass build-up entirely, only ever helps: it lies forward
of the structure CG, so 3 g of it cuts the ballast to 2.46 g.

Ballast is not the whole story. Best L/D is nearly indifferent to all of the
above — it moves 6.32 to 6.60 across every arm — and is set instead by the
speed the polar is read at, 5.87 at 4 m/s against 6.96 at 8 m/s. Dihedral and
the fuselage cross-section exponent are negligible for anything computed here,
though dihedral is a roll-axis device being judged on a pitch-axis result and no
lateral case has been run.

Two assumptions cannot be swung inside this model. The first is `AeroBuildup`
with NeuralFoil section data standing in for a square-cut foam plate at
Re 3.6 × 10⁴: the sweep above only substitutes smooth NACA sections, while the
real leading edge separates at once, so the best L/D here is optimistic by an
amount this chapter cannot bound. The second is that the airframe is rigid and
true, when the plan's own trimming instructions are to warp the fin.
